packages.one_line: Frozen numpy-backed message dataclasses every package joins on
packages.summary: The standard robot data types (ROS's geometry, sensor, trajectory and vision messages) as frozen Python dataclasses, *with* the functions between them: pose offsets, trajectory interpolation and resampling, point projection, depth to point cloud. `.show()` (Rerun) and `.plot()` (matplotlib) on every type. ROS 2 / bag export as an extra. Strict semver: additive changes only.
packages.use_when: Any pose, transform, joint state, trajectory, limit, image or point cloud. **Never define your own Pose or Trajectory.**

packages.one_line: Generic models by type: actuators, arms, sensors, homing procedures
packages.summary: Generic physical models of part *types* (servos, arms, conveyors, end effectors, sensors), each a ladder of models from ideal to learned (M0 ideal → M1 datasheet → M2 Coulomb + viscous → M3 friction …). Every rung states its parameters, equation and references. No maker, no SKU. Imports robot_msgs and numpy only.
packages.use_when: What parameters a model of an actuator or arm needs, which friction or dynamics model to use, how parameter names map.

packages.one_line: Feed-forward/feedback controllers as black boxes plus a Layout
packages.summary: Controllers as black boxes: a robot_msgs message in, a `ServoCommand` out, `controller.tick(state, dt)`. Joint trajectory controller (Python and C++), joint impedance. Each benchmarked on a ladder of rungs (free motion, fast motion, impacts, pushes, replanning, host stalls) for performance and cost.
packages.use_when: Tracking a trajectory, impedance or compliance, choosing a controller, host vs board control.

packages.one_line: Workspace and IK-branch reach of any arm, FK/IK passed in
packages.summary: Reachability of any arm in Cartesian and joint space, from FK and IK passed in as pure functions. Reach maps, joint maps, IK branches, orientations; save results, view them in viser, and hand them downstream as a `ReachableWorkspace` (`robot_reach.workspace`, from `ReachResult.workspace()`) whose named regions (reachable, top-down, hemisphere, dexterous, your own) sample IK-checked poses. Ready and rest poses: `robot_reach.rest` measures a pose's footprint, clearance and holding power over a scene, and `robot_reach.goals.solve` picks the best one for a use case (a `PoseGoal`: clearances, held or limp, readiness to a workspace, energy), whose record `to_named_pose` turns into a robot_msgs NamedPose. Example arms built in (pendulum, RR, five-bar, 3-DOF shoulder, UR5e); loads URDFs.
packages.use_when: Workspace, "can the arm reach X", IK branch choice, sampling reachable poses for a task, placing a robot or a bin, arm sizing, choosing a ready or rest pose (and its NamedPose).

packages.one_line: Motor and board heat tracking with burst-limit decisions
packages.summary: Running servo motors above their continuous rating in short bursts, safely. v1: an I²t burst budget per drive plus a hard cut on board temperature. v2: a lumped thermal network per drive, fed by logged current, with a Kalman observer. Standard library at runtime.
packages.use_when: Motor or board heat, burst limits, duty cycles, how hard a joint may be pushed.

packages.one_line: Trajectory kinds from limits and tasks, one JointTrajectory out
packages.summary: A signal library for robot motion. Every trajectory kind is a `TrajectoryGenerator`: a plain function `f(JointSpace, numbers/points/poses) → JointTrajectory`, inside the limits and at rest at both ends. ~80 kinds: moves, waypoints (joint and Cartesian), random waypoints, pick and place, chirps, multisines, PRBS, step trains, PID tuning, friction ID, ISO 9283 tests, workspace sweeps, moving targets. `chain` / `split` to compose. The legs inside a kind are timed by a `WaypointTrajectoryGenerator` (points + joint limits in, a JointTrajectory out: minimum_jerk, trapezoid, ruckig, ruckig_pro, toppra as plugins), passed as `waypoint_generator=`. The robot (limits, FK/IK, dynamics, collision) is injected via `JointSpace`.
packages.use_when: Generating any motion: test trajectories, excitation for system ID, pick-and-place paths, tuning signals, benchmarks.

packages.one_line: Counts human interventions per working hour; ranks causes
packages.summary: A library that counts working hours between human interventions, from every source (chat asks, logs, faults, tickets), and ranks their causes as a to-do list. Its loop (`AutonomyAgent.tick`) is plain code with no model in it: it ingests every source, scores the KPI and verifies each fix by measuring its cause go down.
packages.use_when: Measuring and driving down human interventions; autonomy KPIs.

packages.one_line: Tracking, stop, lag, repeatability metrics over message streams
packages.summary: Performance metrics for robot parts: tracking error, stop error, lag, repeatability, with units. Works on a whole recording or a live feed, with identical numbers. Runs group into rungs, stations and deployments; pass/fail targets (objectives) are kept apart from the maths. Shaped like torchmetrics.
packages.use_when: Scoring any run: target vs real, sim vs real, before vs after, pass/fail gates.

packages.one_line: Per-robot and fleet activity, work queue, stalemate flags
packages.summary: A library that measures whether each robot is doing useful work (claimed, active, moving), keeps a work queue moving, flags stalemates and gives every idle second a reason. Its loop (`ActivityAgent.tick`) is plain code with no model in it: it prompts the owners of the work and never decides what the work is.
packages.use_when: Fleet or robot utilisation, uptime dashboards, work queues.

packages.one_line: A/B trajectory comparison report; a runs workbench over many sites; trajectory and grasp coverage viewers
packages.summary: Viewers on robot_msgs types, in three parts. Comparison: a turn-key A/B trajectory viewer that writes one static `report.html` (target vs sim vs real). Trajectory coverage (`traj_compare.coverage`: how much of a robot's joint limits, workspace and tool orientations a set of trajectories visits) and grasp coverage (`traj_compare.grasp_coverage`: how much of a gripper's jaw range, approach directions, rolls and offered area a set of GraspPose uses, and where the failures sat), each one payload feeding a data-ui workbench, Matplotlib, Viser and W&B; grasp coverage is also deployed as its own grasp dataset viewer (`grasp_viewer` link). Coverage of any list of dataclass records moved to its own package, dataclass_coverage.
packages.use_when: Comparing runs (target vs sim vs real, before vs after), benchmark reports, "how much of the space does this trajectory or grasp dataset cover?". **Never write a bespoke trajectory plot or coverage page.**

packages.one_line: A stock Rerun viewer for every robot_msgs type: show, save or stream, each with a preconfigured blueprint
packages.summary: One curated Rerun view per robot_msgs type (blueprint, sample data, screenshot) on top of robot_msgs' own logger: `viz.show(msg)`, `viz.save(path, msg)`, `with viz.stream("arm") as live: live.log(msg)`, `viz.blueprint(...)` for your own recording. The landing page lists every type (supported ones clickable) and every use-case dashboard plugins add, each with Open in browser / Open on desktop.
packages.use_when: Looking at any robot_msgs message in Rerun, live or from a file. **Never hand-write a Rerun layout for a standard type; grow its view here.**

packages.one_line: RobotTwin, calibrate() and fit/replay over real or simulated runs
packages.summary: The outer API on top of everything: digital twins (`RobotTwin`), one-click `.calibrate()` (configure → fit → tune → measure routines), MuJoCo simulation, and dashboards of how close each twin is to its real hardware. May import every package above.
packages.use_when: Twins, calibration, system identification, sim-vs-real comparison, the one-call API over a whole robot.

packages.one_line: Diagnostics as pure functions: diagnose(config, data) -> Result
packages.summary: Robot Diagnostics (RobotDx). Diagnostics as checks: a diagnostic = a metric + a threshold, with a registry, records (ROS `DiagnosticStatus` shape), roll-ups and ~33 stock checks: tracking and stop error, ISO 9283, frequency response, fidelity, coverage, feedback, health, camera, events. JTC diagnostics (`stock.jtc`): one causal per-tick monitor over target, command and measured state (ros2 JTC tolerances, command sent, tick timing, torque residual, blocked / contact / collision, servo timeout and fault), the same numbers live and on a replay. Stdlib-only core; the stock maths (numpy, robot_metrics, sim2real) is the `stock` extra, imported lazily. The io-diagnostics app (dashboard, device tree) uses it.
packages.use_when: Is this robot, joint or sensor healthy? Pass/fail checks on runs, health dashboards, turning a metric into an alarm. A joint trajectory controller's per-tick diagnostics and collision detection.

packages.one_line: Components, ports and systems in Python or C++, over dora; robot_msgs on the wire
packages.summary: The communication API: components with ports, systems that wire them from outside, deployments in one process or across the network, over two backends (`inproc` threads and dora-rs 0.5). A component can also be C++, written against one header (`cpp/include/like_keras/lk.hpp`) and built with CMake's `lk_component()` into a `.so` that runs as a dora node or as a GIL-free real-time thread inside a Python process (`like_keras.native`). The frozen v0 contract is `docs/CONTRACT.md`.
packages.use_when: Connecting robot components, sensors and processes; dataflows; a C++ real-time controller that swaps in for a Python one in one line.

languages.evidence: 6 headers: abi, lk, msgs/control, msgs/sensor +2 more

packages.one_line: Allowed Collision Matrix for any robot, robots, or robot + scene
packages.summary: Computes the Allowed Collision Matrix (SRDF disable_collisions) for one robot, several robots, or a robot and its scene: a robot description, or your own pure FK function plus bodies, in; a robot_msgs AllowedCollisionMatrix out, proved equal to brute force. Closed linkages (five-bar, delta) work through the description's own expand(q). Viewed in viser with a floating matrix window.
packages.use_when: Which link pairs to collision-check, generating an SRDF, viewing a robot's collision pairs.

types.name: Msg
types.what: Base of every message

types.name: Comparison
types.what: What `robot_msgs.compare.compare(reference, measured)` returns

types.name: Dataset
types.what: Runs with unique names, and a `title`

types.name: DatasetComparison
types.what: What `compare_dataset(dataset)` returns: one `RunComparison` per run, by run name

types.name: ErrorStats
types.what: Summary of one error signal over its finite samples, in the signal's own SI unit

types.name: JointTolerance
types.what: control_msgs/JointTolerance: limits on one joint's ``|reference - measured|``

types.name: Outcome
types.what: The verdict: a ``FollowJointTrajectory`` result code, the reason, and the room left

types.name: PoseTolerance
types.what: Limits on a pose error's magnitudes: ``position`` (m) and ``rotation`` angle (rad)

types.name: Recording
types.what: Every stream one source recorded in one run, by stream name

types.name: Run
types.what: One run of one experiment: every source's `Recording`, and which pairs to compare

types.name: RunComparison
types.what: What `compare_run(run)` returns: one `Comparison` per pair and shared stream

types.name: Tolerances
types.what: What a run must stay inside, as ``joint_trajectory_controller`` states it

types.name: Violation
types.what: One limit broken, at the first sample that broke it

types.name: EffortStall
types.what: Done when `joint` moves slower than `speed` while its measured effort pushes the way its setpoint runs with more than `effort` (N·m or N), for `dwell` seconds: it is pressing something

types.name: Elapsed
types.what: Done when the step has run `duration` seconds

types.name: JointCommand
types.what: What one joint does during one step

types.name: JointCommandSequence
types.what: A recipe read top to bottom: `steps` are `JointCommandStep`s or (0.8) the primitives `Command`, `Delay`, `Condition`; lists inside `steps` are flattened, so helper calls compose directly: `JointCommandSequence(steps=[find_hardstop(...), move_to(...)])`

types.name: JointCommandSequenceController
types.what: Runs `sequence`; see the module docstring

types.name: JointCommandStep
types.what: One step: a `JointCommand` per joint it names, done when ANY of `done_when` holds, the whole sequence aborted if not done within `timeout` (s)

types.name: Reached
types.what: Done when every listed joint's setpoint is at its target and the joint is within `tolerance` of it, slower than `speed`, for `dwell` seconds

types.name: ServoCommand
types.what: Targets for servo `name[i]`, in SI

types.name: ServoState
types.what: `position[i]` (rad or m), `velocity[i]`, `effort[i]` (N·m or N) belong to servo `name[i]`

types.name: Settled
types.what: Done when every listed joint has moved slower than `speed` for `dwell` seconds

types.name: Stall
types.what: Done when `joint`'s setpoint leads it by more than `lead` (in the direction of motion) while it moves slower than `speed`, for `dwell` seconds: something stopped it

types.name: CoverageResult
types.what: The coverage of one point set over one grid

types.name: FiducialArray
types.what: `header` is the image's: its `stamp` is the capture time (mid-exposure when known) and its `frame_id` the camera's optical frame, so a solver can join the markers to the robot's `JointState` at the same stamp and to the camera's `CameraInfo` by frame

types.name: FiducialBoard
types.what: A board of `cols` × `rows`, `header.frame_id` its frame

types.name: FiducialDetection
types.what: One marker in one image

types.name: FiducialMap
types.what: `mounts`, one per marker; a marker key ``(dictionary, id)`` appears once (two physical copies of one marker cannot be told apart by a detector, so a map refuses them)

types.name: FiducialMount
types.what: One marker, placed: `pose` is ``T_parent_marker``, the marker frame (`marker_object_points`) in `header.frame_id` — a robot link, a board, the world

types.name: FiducialPose
types.what: `pose` is ``T_camera_marker``: the marker frame (`marker_object_points`) in the enclosing `FiducialArray`'s camera frame (``header.frame_id``, the optical frame: x right, y down, z forward)

types.name: FiducialTrack
types.what: `pose` is the marker frame in the enclosing `FiducialTrackArray`'s frame

types.name: FiducialTrackArray
types.what: `header.stamp` is the estimate's time, `header.frame_id` the frame every pose is in (the robot base, the world)

types.name: Accel
types.what: Linear and angular acceleration of a body, both in the frame the header names

types.name: Inertia
types.what: Mass `m` (kg), centre of mass `com` (m) and the six independent tensor entries (kg·m²)

types.name: Point
types.what: Metres

types.name: Pose
types.what: Same maths as `Transform` (every method converts and delegates), different intent: a Pose says where something *is*, a Transform says how to move between frames

types.name: Pose2D
types.what: Metres and radians; `theta` is the heading about +Z, stored as given (not wrapped)

types.name: PoseStamped
types.what: A pose with a frame and a time: ROS ``geometry_msgs/PoseStamped``

types.name: Quaternion
types.what: Unit quaternions are rotations; the fields are stored exactly as given

types.name: Transform
types.what: ``T_parent_child``: maps points expressed in the child frame into the parent frame

types.name: TransformStamped
types.what: ``header.frame_id`` is the parent frame; `transform` maps `child_frame_id` into it

types.name: Twist
types.what: Linear and angular velocity of a body, both in the frame the header names

types.name: Vector3
types.what: Metres, m/s, newtons

types.name: Wrench
types.what: Force (N) and torque (N·m) applied to a body, both in the frame the header names

types.name: AllowedCollisionMatrix
types.what: Pairwise allowed-contact matrix over named bodies (robot links and scene objects)

types.name: CollisionElement
types.what: One thing in a `CollisionScene`: moveit_msgs/CollisionObject's geometry plus its tags

types.name: CollisionScene
types.what: Every collision element of a scene, in one frame (`header.frame_id`, usually ``"world"``)

types.name: GraspPose
types.what: Where the gripper's tool frame goes to grasp, and how wide its jaws are

types.name: NamedPose
types.what: A saved position of a robot's joint group, looked up by name (``"ready"``, ``"home"``)

types.name: Waypoint
types.what: A tool pose to pass through, in the `WaypointAction`'s frame, plus what happens there

types.name: WaypointAction
types.what: The waypoints in order, all in `header.frame_id`, for the tool frame `tool_frame`

types.name: CameraInfo
types.what: Image size, camera matrix `k`, distortion `d`, rectification `r`, projection `p`

types.name: Image
types.what: `data` is (H, W) or (H, W, C) in the dtype `encoding` names; the dtype is kept as is

types.name: Imu
types.what: Angular velocity in rad/s, linear acceleration in m/s², both in `header.frame_id`

types.name: JointState
types.what: `position[i]` (rad or m), `velocity[i]` and `effort[i]` belong to joint `name[i]`

types.name: PointCloud
types.what: `points` is (N, 3) float32 in `header.frame_id`; each channel has leading dimension N

types.name: Mesh
types.what: `vertices` is ``(N, 3)`` float64 metres; `triangles` is ``(M, 3)`` int32 vertex indices (ROS's ``MeshTriangle.vertex_indices``), counter-clockwise seen from outside

types.name: Plane
types.what: `coef` = ``(a, b, c, d)``: the points with ``a·x + b·y + c·z + d = 0``, in the frame the owner names

types.name: SolidPrimitive
types.what: `type` is one of the ROS constants below and `dimensions` follows ROS's index layout:

types.name: Space
types.what: A message seen as a space (gymnasium-style), derived from the instance itself

types.name: ColorRGBA
types.what: Red, green, blue and alpha, each a float in 0..1 (alpha 1 is opaque)

types.name: DiagnosticRecord
types.what: One evaluation of one component's health, sent periodically

types.name: Header
types.what: `stamp` is seconds since the Unix epoch (or since sim start); `frame_id` names the frame

types.name: LogRecord
types.what: One log line from a running component, as it crosses a process or lands in a recording

types.name: Metrics
types.what: `values[i]` (float64) is the metric `names[i]`, as `path` measured it at `header.stamp`

types.name: ImageTrajectory
types.what: Frames `(N, H, W[, C])` of one `encoding` (a sensor_msgs/image_encodings name, as `Image`)

types.name: ImageTrajectoryPoint
types.what: One frame of an `ImageTrajectory`; `image` is it as a sensor `Image`

types.name: ImuTrajectory
types.what: `orientations (N, 4)` xyzw, `angular_velocities (N, 3)` rad/s, `linear_accelerations (N, 3)` m/s², all in `header.frame_id` (the IMU's frame), as sensor_msgs/Imu

types.name: ImuTrajectoryPoint
types.what: One sample of an `ImuTrajectory`

types.name: JointLimitViolation
types.what: One joint past one bound of its `JointLimits` during a run, over every sample past it

types.name: JointLimits
types.what: One value per joint for each bound that is known; `None` means unbounded

types.name: JointTrajectory
types.what: Joint-space motion keyed by joint name

types.name: JointTrajectoryPoint
types.what: trajectory_msgs/JointTrajectoryPoint; `t` is ROS's `time_from_start`

types.name: PoseTrajectory
types.what: `positions (N, 3)` in metres, `orientations (N, 4)` xyzw, optional twist per sample

types.name: PoseTrajectoryPoint
types.what: One sample of a `PoseTrajectory`: position (m), orientation (xyzw) and optional twist

types.name: ServoCommandTrajectory
types.what: Targets sent to servos `joint_names` over time; every per-sample array is ``(N, J)``

types.name: ServoCommandTrajectoryPoint
types.what: One sample of a `ServoCommandTrajectory`: every servo's targets at `t`

types.name: ServoStateTrajectory
types.what: What servos `joint_names` reported over time; every per-sample array is ``(N, J)``

types.name: ServoStateTrajectoryPoint
types.what: One sample of a `ServoStateTrajectory`: every servo's reading at `t`

types.name: Trajectory
types.what: Samples at strictly increasing times `t` (seconds after `header.stamp`)

types.name: TrajectoryPoint
types.what: One sample: its time and the value of every per-sample field at that time

types.name: WrenchTrajectory
types.what: `forces (N, 3)` in N and `torques (N, 3)` in N·m, in `header.frame_id`

types.name: WrenchTrajectoryPoint
types.what: One sample of a `WrenchTrajectory`: `force` (N) and `torque` (N·m)

types.name: BoundingBox2D
types.what: `center` is the box centre in pixels with rotation `center.theta`; sizes are in pixels

types.name: BoundingBox3D
types.what: `center` is the box pose in the parent frame; `size` is the extent along its own x, y, z

types.name: Detection2D
types.what: `results` are the class hypotheses for the box; `id` tracks the object across frames

types.name: Detection2DArray
types.what: The detections of one frame; `header` is the image's header

types.name: Detection3D
types.what: `results` are the class hypotheses for the box; `id` tracks the object across frames

types.name: Detection3DArray
types.what: The detections of one frame; `header` is the sensor frame's header

types.name: ObjectHypothesis
types.what: `class_id` names the class (a label or an id string); `score` is the confidence

types.name: ObjectHypothesisWithPose
types.what: `covariance` is the (6, 6) pose covariance ordered x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw, or `None`
